name: Fast spark oscillator and receiver
summary: Hertz's induction-coil spark generator and small adjustable spark-gap receiver, which revealed very fast electrical oscillations and made electromagnetic waves detectable.
description: Induction-coil-driven spark oscillators and nearly closed secondary conductors with small adjustable gaps reveal rapid electrical oscillations; conductor placement is revised for dielectric tests.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.
why: An unexpected spark effect, which Hertz said theory could not have foreseen, set him on to this apparatus.

date.basis: Hertz dates the triggering observation to spring 1886 and the dielectric-test result to 10 November 1887.

events.statement: Induction-coil-driven spark oscillators and nearly closed secondary conductors with small adjustable gaps reveal rapid electrical oscillations; conductor placement is revised for dielectric tests.
events.caveats: Not a radio communication system. Initial spark discovery was contingent; Hertz explicitly says an essential spark property could not have been foreseen by theory.

evidence.supports: 1886 starting point, spark conditions, secondary gaps and revision of 1887 dielectric geometry.

links.statement: The dielectric-polarization problem guided Hertz’s choice and revision of primary/secondary conductor geometry and insulator insertion tests after a chance spark observation provided a usable method.
links.scope: Karlsruhe, 1886–1887 apparatus development for the 1879 test programme.
links.alternatives: Hertz initially considered Leyden jars/open coils and abandoned the attempt; later unexpected side-sparks supplied a different practical route.
links.caveats: Theory shaped the experimental question and geometry; it did not predict all crucial spark properties or uniquely specify the apparatus.
links.timing: The receiving development follows the source development.
